reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that causal inference must be grounded in both structural validity and empirical verification. The G3 gate enforces that only those causal claims which pass a rigorous identifiability test are accepted. This prevents spurious causality from being reported when the underlying causal graph is insufficiently constrained. The intervention outcome primitive tracks whether a causal claim was truly identified or merely associated, distinguishing between valid causal inference and mere correlation. The causal identification primitive ensures that any causal claim meets the Shpitser-Pearl criteria before being considered valid. Together, these primitives form a closed-loop system where each step validates the next, preventing erroneous conclusions from propagating through the causal chain. Failure occurs when either the graph structure is misidentified or the empirical verification fails, leading to a refusal that halts further processing.
